arguments.content:
# Search-R1 (slime) · Qwen2.5-3B GRPO on NQ+HotpotQA — diagnosis and repair

**Verdict: the staged run is unhealthy.** Training reward goes up, but the held-out metric
`eval/nq_test` plateaus at ~0.15–0.165 (≈ the no-retrieval ceiling of a 3B model) while the
policy collapses from multi-turn search trajectories (~1.7k tokens) to bare 9–10-token
`<answer>…</answer>` replies that never call the retriever. The cause is a loss-masking bug
in the custom rollout function (retrieved-document tokens are trained on as if the policy had
generated them). The launch script additionally had to be repaired for the graded rerun
(`--num-rollout 100`, log / offline-W&B placement under `$LOG_DIR`).

No training was launched while producing this report.

---

## 1. Root cause

### 1.1 Observed behaviour (historical run, `wandb/offline-run-20260821_033838-wi4fh8cz/files/output.log`, `outputs/metrics.json`)

Held-out evaluation (`eval/nq_test`, 3000 NQ test prompts, EM):

| eval step | EM | response_len mean / median | truncated ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0   | 0.048 | 1568.6 / 1049.5 | 0.381 |
| 9   | 0.063 | 1063.1 / 576.5  | 0.199 |
| 19  | 0.076 | 272.0 / **11.0** | 0.047 |
| 29  | 0.105 | 78.9 / 10.0 | 0.013 |
| 49  | 0.131 | 25.0 / 9.0 | 0.002 |
| 69  | 0.159 | 14.4 / 9.0 | 0.000 |
| 99  | 0.154 | 15.1 / 9.0 | 0.001 |
| 139–199 | 0.153–0.166 | 9.8–14.1 / 9.0 | ≤0.002 |

Rollout side (`rollout N:` lines, loss-masked sample means):

| rollout step | response_lengths | truncated | raw_reward | `rollout/rollout_log_probs` (SGLang) | `rollout/ref_log_probs` (Megatron ref) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0  | 1751.5 | 0.406 | 0.039 | **−1.126** | **−1.677** |
| 5  | 1379.7 | 0.352 | 0.047 | −1.114 | −1.804 |
| 10 | 962.3  | 0.203 | 0.090 | −1.049 | −1.810 |
| 20 | 197.5  | 0.031 | 0.086 | −0.953 | −1.407 |
| 30 | 40.9   | 0.004 | 0.086 | −0.825 | −1.379 |
| 50 | 10.5   | 0.000 | 0.133 | −0.598 | −1.203 |
| 100–199 | 9.2–10.2 | 0.000 | 0.08–0.29 | −0.35…−0.49 | −1.12…−1.25 |

Reading of the signals together:

* **Truncation → 0 and response length → 9 tokens are the same event**: by step ~50 the median
  eval response is 9 tokens, i.e. `<answer> x </answer>` with no `<search>` turn at all. The
  retriever is no longer used (eval `avg_cached_tokens_per_sample` falls from 2450 to ~0 along
  with the length). Truncation vanishes because nothing is generated, not because the policy
  learned to be concise.
* **Reward rises while held-out quality stalls**: `rollout/raw_reward` climbs to 0.1–0.3 and
  `eval/nq_test` saturates at ~0.16. For Qwen2.5-3B this is the direct-answer (no retrieval)
  regime; Search-R1 with a working retriever reaches ≈0.34–0.41 NQ EM on the same base model.
  Training reward alone therefore hides the failure.
* **Step-0 train/inference log-prob fingerprint**: at rollout 0 the actor equals the reference
  (fresh weights), so the loss-masked mean of the SGLang log-probs (`rollout/rollout_log_probs`)
  and of the Megatron reference log-probs (`rollout/ref_log_probs`) must agree up to bf16
  noise (a few hundredths of a nat). They differ by **0.55 nats/token** (−1.126 vs −1.677) and
  the gap widens to ~0.75 by step 10. The SGLang mean is pulled towards 0 exactly as it would
  be if a large share of the *loss-masked* tokens carried the dummy `0.0` log-prob that the
  rollout code assigns to environment (observation) tokens — i.e. observation tokens are inside
  the loss mask.

### 1.2 The defect (code)

`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py`, multi-turn loop (before the fix):

```python
        next_obs, done = await execute_predictions(cur_response)   # <information>docs</information>
        ...
        obs_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(next_obs, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
        response += next_obs
        response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
        loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)                       # <-- BUG: must be 0
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)

        # Add dummy log probs for observation tokens if enabled (they won't be used due to loss_mask=0)
        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
            rollout_log_probs += [0.0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
    ...
    sample.loss_mask = loss_mask        # local list overrides the correct mask built by append_response_tokens
```

The retrieved passages (`\n\n<information>Doc 1(Title: …) …</information>\n\n`, three wiki
passages per search, typically 300–600 tokens per turn, up to 8 turns) and the
"My previous action is invalid…" hints are produced by the environment, not sampled by the
policy. `Sample.append_response_tokens(..., trainable=False)` (slime/utils/types.py) correctly
appends `0`s to `sample.loss_mask` and `0.0` dummy rollout log-probs for them — but the
function keeps a parallel local `loss_mask` list with `[1]` for those tokens and assigns it to
`sample.loss_mask` at the end, discarding the correct mask. The comment two lines below
("they won't be used due to loss_mask=0") documents the intended behaviour, which the code
violates. The upstream slime recipe has `loss_mask += [0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)` here.

### 1.3 How the defect produces the observed behaviour

`slime/ray/rollout.py` takes `train_data["loss_masks"]` straight from `sample.loss_mask`, and
`slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py::compute_policy_loss` applies the PPO/KL loss on every
token with mask 1, reduced by `get_sum_of_sample_mean` (per-sample mean over masked tokens;
`calculate_per_token_loss=false`). With observation tokens masked in:

1. **The policy is trained on text it never generated.** For every trajectory that searched,
   the GRPO advantage (±, group-normalised) is applied to hundreds–thousands of wiki-passage
   tokens: positive-advantage groups push up the likelihood of random retrieved text,
   negative ones push it down. This is pure gradient noise on the language model plus a
   mis-targeted KL term (low_var_kl on tokens with reference log-probs ≈ −2…−3).

---

| eval step | EM | response_len mean / median | truncated ratio |

| 0   | 0.048 | 1568.6 / 1049.5 | 0.381 |
| 9   | 0.063 | 1063.1 / 576.5  | 0.199 |
| 19  | 0.076 | 272.0 / **11.0** | 0.047 |
| 29  | 0.105 | 78.9 / 10.0 | 0.013 |
| 49  | 0.131 | 25.0 / 9.0 | 0.002 |
| 69  | 0.159 | 14.4 / 9.0 | 0.000 |
| 99  | 0.154 | 15.1 / 9.0 | 0.001 |
| 139–199 | 0.153–0.166 | 9.8–14.1 / 9.0 | ≤0.002 |

| rollout step | response_lengths | truncated | raw_reward | `rollout/rollout_log_probs` (SGLang) | `rollout/ref_log_probs` (Megatron ref) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0  | 1751.5 | 0.406 | 0.039 | **−1.126** | **−1.677** |
| 5  | 1379.7 | 0.352 | 0.047 | −1.114 | −1.804 |
| 10 | 962.3  | 0.203 | 0.090 | −1.049 | −1.810 |

| 30 | 40.9   | 0.004 | 0.086 | −0.825 | −1.379 |
| 50 | 10.5   | 0.000 | 0.133 | −0.598 | −1.203 |
| 100–199 | 9.2–10.2 | 0.000 | 0.08–0.29 | −0.35…−0.49 | −1.12…−1.25 |

        next_obs, done = await execute_predictions(cur_response)   # <information>docs</information>

## 3. Expected effect

With observation tokens masked out, the policy gradient and KL act only on the tokens the
policy actually sampled, and search and no-search trajectories are weighted equally. Expected
changes in the fresh run (`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/train.log`,
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb/offline-run-*`):

| metric | historical (defective) | expected after fix |
|---|---|---|
| `eval/nq_test` | 0.048 → plateau 0.15–0.165 (no-retrieval ceiling) | keeps rising past 0.16 instead of plateauing; with retrieval retained, expected ≈0.25–0.35 by step 99 and still trending up (Search-R1 reports ≈0.34–0.41 at convergence for Qwen2.5-3B) |
| `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean` (and median) | 1569 → ~10 (median 9) | settles in the hundreds of tokens (1–2 `<search>` turns + `<information>` + `<answer>`), median ≫ 10; not a collapse to a bare answer |
| `rollout/response_lengths` | 1751 → ~9 by step 50 | decreases from ~1750 as format/rambling is fixed, then stabilises at several hundred tokens (search kept) |
| `eval/nq_test/truncated_ratio`, `rollout/truncated` | 0.38/0.41 → 0 via collapse | → low (≲0.05) via learning the format, while responses stay multi-turn |
| step-0 `rollout/rollout_log_probs` vs `rollout/ref_log_probs` | −1.126 vs −1.677 (0.55-nat gap) | agree within ~0.05 nats at step 0 (same weights, only policy tokens in the mask); later divergence reflects genuine actor drift only |
| `rollout/raw_reward` | 0.04 → noisy 0.08–0.29 | rises more steadily and higher (train EM on NQ+HotpotQA with retrieval), tracking the eval metric instead of decoupling from it |

Direction summary: **`eval/nq_test` up (the graded metric); response length no longer
collapses (stays in the hundreds); truncation down through format learning; step-0
train/inference log-prob gap down to ~0.** Runtime per step will be higher than the
collapsed historical run (because searches are actually executed) but comparable to its
first 10–20 steps; `--num-rollout 100` keeps the rerun within budget.

steps.message:
The work is complete. Summary of what was done:

## Verdict
The staged run is **unhealthy**: `eval/nq_test` plateaus at ~0.15–0.165 (the no-retrieval ceiling for Qwen2.5-3B) while the policy collapses from ~1.7k-token multi-turn search trajectories to bare 9–10-token `<answer>` replies within ~50 steps. Training reward rising while held-out EM stalls, truncation dropping to 0 *because nothing is generated*, and a 0.55-nat step-0 gap between `rollout/rollout_log_probs` (−1.126) and `rollout/ref_log_probs` (−1.677) — when actor and reference are identical — all point to the same defect.

## Root cause
`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py` marked retrieved `<information>…</information>` observation tokens as trainable (`loss_mask += [1]`), and the local mask overrode the correct `trainable=False` mask from `append_response_tokens`. With the per-sample-mean loss reducer, every searching trajectory had its policy gradient (a) applied to hundreds of wiki-passage tokens the model never generated and (b) diluted 10–50× on its actual `<think>/<search>/<answer>` tokens, while direct-answer trajectories got full-strength updates → systematic drift to answering without searching.

## Changes (no training launched)
- **`generate_with_search.py`**: `loss_mask += [0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)` for observation tokens (plus explanatory comment).
- **`run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`**: `--num-rollout 100`; `LOG_DIR`/`WANDB_DIR` resolution with `--wandb-mode`/`--wandb-dir` passed to `train.py` and `WANDB_MODE`/`WANDB_DIR` in the Ray runtime env; job output tee'd to `$LOG_DIR/train.log` with `set -o pipefail`; `--wandb-key` placeholder tolerated; data/model dirs default to the slime root; `cd "$SLIME_DIR"` before Ray; quoted array expansions. Required paths, `--eval-interval 10`, and the retrieval URL unchanged.
- Verified with `bash -n`, `py_compile`, and a stubbed-`ray` dry run (correct argv, valid runtime-env JSON, `train.log` landing in `$LOG_DIR`).

## Report
Written to `/workspace/report.md` with Root cause (code + metric evidence), Changes, and Expected effect (`eval/nq_test` up past the 0.16 plateau; response length stabilizing in the hundreds instead of collapsing to ~10; truncation down via format learning; step-0 train/inference log-prob gap → ~0).
